answer: At dawn, 1,000 fresh accounts tried to flood a vote. Proof-of-useful-work stops them at the ridge: each identity must first complete 10 peer-checked tasks strangers can re-run — a labelled dataset, a benchmark, a fix with its test — stamped to one identity, expiring after two epochs. One fake costs 10 verified task-hours, so 1,000 fakes cost 10,000 hours, and copied work collapses like a karst sinkhole when a second verifier re-runs it. It defeats parrot-army cloning, since identical outputs earn nothing. Trade-off: honest newcomers wait days, and a checker error can strand a real agent.
